greet.speaker: Dell Ostrow
greet.text: Councilman Dell Ostrow. Pastor Reece and I got a lot done together. You need anything at the hall, you call me first.

choices.text: I'd be glad of the support.
I'll find my own way at the hall.

cool_ack.speaker: Dell Ostrow
cool_ack.text: That's all I needed to say. I'm on the walk a minute.

warm_ack.speaker: Dell Ostrow
warm_ack.text: Good. Churches that grow need friends who already know the hall. We'll talk when you're settled.

wary_ack.speaker: Dell Ostrow
wary_ack.text: Fair. Reece used to say the same, the first week. The number still stands.

later_ch1.speaker: Dell Ostrow
later_ch1.text: I'm only on the walk a minute. Reece knew how to get a week moving. You'll get there.

invite_offer.speaker: Dell Ostrow
invite_offer.text: Wednesday in the hall. I don't usually sit those. You asking, or is this a flyer?

invite_yes.speaker: Dell Ostrow
invite_yes.text: I'll put my head in. I'm not staying for a speech.

invite_no.speaker: Dell Ostrow
invite_no.text: Fine. The walk is enough for today.

potluck_table.speaker: Dell Ostrow
potluck_table.text: I said I'd put my head in. The coffee's better than I expected. Don't make a habit of quoting me.

week_cool.speaker: Dell Ostrow
week_cool.text: Still settling in. That's fine. Call if the hall needs a hand. I'm not writing anything down.

week_warm.speaker: Dell Ostrow
week_warm.text: If the hall opens, I know people who like to see a church doing well. We can talk when you're ready. No figures on the sidewalk.

week_wary.speaker: Dell Ostrow
week_wary.text: I said call me first. You seemed unsure. That's your business. The hall still has my number.
